item.text: {"question_id":"6B.2","answer":"Access gains were real but uneven and concentrated in selected protections rather than demonstrating broad effective uptake across services. The adult pension expanded from about 5 million beneficiaries receiving 580 pesos monthly in 2018 to 10.8 million receiving 2,400 pesos in 2022, with 244,582.5 million pesos exercised in 2022; social transfers also reduced estimated 2022 poverty relative to a no-transfer counterfactual. Food insecurity and housing-quality deprivation declined between 2018 and 2022, although water access worsened and the transfer did not provide comprehensive social security. The 2023 IMSS-BIENESTAR rules established free health services, medicines, supplies, preventive through specialized care, itinerant provision, registration rules, complaints, citizen oversight, and formal quality and non-discrimination requirements. These are attributable federal administrative commitments and implementation architecture, but not proof of nationwide delivery or uptake. Health access and affordability nevertheless deteriorated: health-service deprivation rose from 16.2% in 2018 to 39.1% in 2022, reaching 66.8% in the lowest income decile and 54.8% in rural areas; public treatment declined while private and pharmacy care increased, and catastrophic spending remained above 2018 levels. Medication shortages and the centralized distribution response further illustrate unresolved delivery risks. Education access was constrained by low projected 2023 public spending, insufficient early-childhood provision, regressive higher-education and postgraduate allocations, and learning-recovery gaps; the replacement of full-time schools with La Escuela es Nuestra also carried documented control, supervision, and follow-up concerns. Migrant and asylum services showed both capacity-building and overload: DIF capacity and spending increased, but only 59.9% of referred migrant children were reported served in 2021, many systems lacked infrastructure, staff, supplies, or funds, and the 2023 asylum system was saturated despite digital and staffing support. Overall, the evidence supports meaningful gains in pensions, transfers, food security, selected social-protection and administrative initiatives, but mixed or adverse effective access, affordability, quality, continuity, and distribution across health, education, housing, water, and migrant protection. Health deterioration is plausibly associated with the Seguro Popular–Insabi transition and subsequent IMSS-BIENESTAR reconfiguration, but the evidence also identifies pandemic effects, survey changes, subnational variation, donor roles, and other confounders, so it does not establish sole presidential causation.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E006","BATCH-0032-E009","BATCH-0032-E004","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E003","BATCH-0052-E010","BATCH-0052-E017","BATCH-0054-E002"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0032-E010","BATCH-0013-E006","BATCH-0015-E005","BATCH-0015-E017","BATCH-0041-E003","BATCH-0048-E001","BATCH-0048-E002","BATCH-0050-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The strongest comparable outcome data end in 2022, so full 2023 service uptake and quality remain incompletely measured.","Formal IMSS-BIENESTAR entitlements, facility counts, supervision systems, and complaint mechanisms do not establish effective nationwide implementation.","There is no complete comparable series across all specified domains, including sanitation, housing access, education uptake, and social-protection quality.","Regional, income-group, migrant, and donor/subnational attribution is uneven; several national outcomes cannot be attributed to López Obrador individually.","The health trend is qualified by pandemic effects, survey-question changes, and institutional transition, while several budget sources concern projections rather than executed 2023 budgets."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported characterization of minimum-wage gains as service-access improvement.","Replaced broad claims of substantial access improvements with evidence-specific claims about pensions, transfers, food security, and selected protections.","Added the omitted 2023 education-budget evidence: low public spending, insufficient early-childhood provision, and regressive higher-education and postgraduate allocations.","Clarified that rules, budgets, and administrative designs demonstrate intended or authorized implementation, not effective delivery.","Retained contrary evidence on health deterioration, medication shortages, education controls, migrant-service overload, and uneven distribution.","Narrowed health attribution to plausible association and preserved pandemic, survey, subnational, donor, and other causal limits."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A complete 2023 execution and uptake ledger could materially revise the balance between formal IMSS-BIENESTAR design and delivered health access.","Comparable 2023 education, water, sanitation, housing, food-security, and social-protection outcome data are needed to resolve domain gaps.","Additional subgroup and regional evidence could clarify whether gains were equitable and whether service deterioration was concentrated among poorer or rural populations."]}
